newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's PM Kabariti to visit Gaza on Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's PM Kabariti to visit Gaza on Saturday.

text.p: Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti said on Thursday he would hold talks with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat on Saturday in Gaza to boost bilateral ties and advance Middle East peace.

Kabariti told reporters during a news conference with visiting Qatari Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani that the talks with Arafat in Gaza would tackle obstacles facing peace accords.
The visit, to convene a long delayed meeting of the higher Jordanian-Palestinian committee, is also an attempt to advance bilateral economic and political cooperation.
"I believe that President Arafat and the legitimate elected Palestinian leadership is aware of the (challenges) and our coordination is nearly daily," he added.
Kabariti said the coming few months would be critical because of the scheduled Israeli pullbacks from rural areas in the West Bank under recent Israeli-Palestinian accords.

Kabariti attacked the Islamist-led opposition in Jordan for a decision taken on Wednesday to boycott parliament to protest Amman's stance on Israeli plans to build 6,500 new homes for Jews in Jerusalem.
The vocal opposition, who hold nearly 20 seats in the 80 member parliament, are demanding severing diplomatic ties established after a 1994 peace treaty.
"This is not the picture that we want to give of Jordan and its efforts in pushing the peace process," Kabariti said.

Kabariti stressed Jordan saw dialogue as the only way to get Israel to commit itself to sticking to its pledges, saying any other route would play into the hands of extremists from both sides who wanted to derail peace.

"All possible efforts have to be made to foil the opportunity by any party...Israeli or Arab to attack the peace process... or to give justification that would allow some parties even official not to commit itself to commitments agreed upon," he said.
